tagline: One date table, three relationships, three time perspectives

slides.title: Role-Playing Dimensions
slides.body: A role-playing dimension is a single dimension table connected to a fact table via multiple relationships, each representing a different business concept. The classic example: one DimDate table connected as OrderDate, ShipDate, and DueDate — the same date dimension 'plays three different roles.'
slides.keyPoint: Only ONE relationship between any two tables can be ACTIVE at a time. Additional relationships are INACTIVE (grey dashed). Use USERELATIONSHIP() inside CALCULATE to temporarily activate an inactive one.

slides.title: Three Date Relationships — Only OrderDate is Active
slides.caption: DimDate connects to FactOrders three times. One active (solid), two inactive (dashed). DAX and slicers use OrderDate by default.
slides.filterNote: Without USERELATIONSHIP, all time intelligence functions and date slicers use the active OrderDate relationship.

slides.title: USERELATIONSHIP — Activate ShipDate for One Measure
slides.caption: Switch the active relationship just for this calculation, without changing the model
slides.expression:
Revenue by Ship Date =
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(FactOrders[Revenue]),
        USERELATIONSHIP(
            FactOrders[ShipDateID],
            DimDate[DateID]
        )
    )

-- Inside this CALCULATE:
--  1. Active OrderDateID relationship is DEACTIVATED
--  2. ShipDateID relationship becomes ACTIVE
--  3. Year slicer now filters by ship date
--  4. Original state restored when CALCULATE exits
slides.explanation: USERELATIONSHIP takes the two columns that form the inactive relationship you want to activate. It swaps active/inactive status only within the CALCULATE expression — the model's relationships are unchanged everywhere else.

slides.title: Inside CALCULATE — ShipDate Now Active
slides.caption: USERELATIONSHIP temporarily activates the ShipDate path. OrderDate and DueDate become inactive for this calculation only.
slides.filterNote: USERELATIONSHIP(FactOrders[ShipDateID], DimDate[DateID]) is active. The Year slicer now restricts orders by their ShipDate.

slides.title: PL-300 Exam Traps — Role-Playing Dimensions
bullets: You cannot have two active relationships between the same two tables. Power BI automatically inactivates subsequent relationships and shows them as grey dashed lines.
USERELATIONSHIP must be inside CALCULATE — it cannot be used in a standalone calculated column or as a direct model change.
Time intelligence functions (TOTALYTD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATEADD) use the ACTIVE relationship by default. Wrap them in CALCULATE with USERELATIONSHIP to target an inactive one.
Alternative: duplicate DimDate in Power Query into DimOrderDate, DimShipDate, DimDueDate — all active relationships, no USERELATIONSHIP needed. Trade-off: larger model size.

Exam question: 'Revenue by Ship Date returns the same totals as Revenue by Order Date.' Fix: verify USERELATIONSHIP(FactOrders[ShipDateID], DimDate[DateID]) is inside a CALCULATE expression and both columns are spelled correctly.
slides.keyPoint: Role-playing dimension = one dimension table, multiple relationships to the same fact table, only one active at a time. USERELATIONSHIP inside CALCULATE is the standard pattern to switch between them.
